classification.difficultyReason: Interpret single and double sign changes as reflections, then map marked points, extrema, branches and asymptotic approaches while preserving the supplied curves.

content.prompt: The graph of a function is given. Sketch the required reflection.

spec.description: Qualitative cubic-shaped graph with arrows at both ends; no equation is inferred.
spec.mathematics: Passes through (0,0), local maximum (1,2), marked point (2,1), and local minimum (3,0). Dashed guides at (1,2) and (2,1); x labels 1,2,3 and y labels 1,2. Bezier control coordinates encode the qualitative drawing, not additional numerical givens.

answer.short: Reflection in the $y$-axis. Maximum $(-1,2)$; marked point $(-2,1)$; minimum $(-3,0)$; passes through $(0,0)$.
answer.worked:
Reflect in the $y$-axis using $(x,y)\mapsto(-x,y)$.
$$\begin{aligned}(1,2)&\mapsto(-1,2)\\(2,1)&\mapsto(-2,1)\\(3,0)&\mapsto(-3,0)\\(0,0)&\mapsto(0,0)\end{aligned}$$
The maximum and minimum retain their heights. Mirror the entire curve, including its ends, across the $y$-axis.

spec.description: Complete solution graph obtained by reflecting every base-curve point and control point in the y-axis.
spec.mathematics: Maximum (-1,2), point (-2,1), minimum (-3,0), origin fixed; left end rises and right end falls. Source-required guides and numerical labels retained.

answer.short: Reflection in the $x$-axis. Minimum $(1,-2)$; marked point $(2,-1)$; maximum $(3,0)$; passes through $(0,0)$.
answer.worked:
Reflect in the $x$-axis using $(x,y)\mapsto(x,-y)$.
$$\begin{aligned}(1,2)&\mapsto(1,-2)\\(2,1)&\mapsto(2,-1)\\(3,0)&\mapsto(3,0)\\(0,0)&\mapsto(0,0)\end{aligned}$$
The original maximum becomes a minimum and the original minimum becomes a maximum. Mirror the entire curve across the $x$-axis.

spec.description: Complete solution graph using the exact vertical reflection of the base Bezier curve.
spec.mathematics: Minimum (1,-2), point (2,-1), maximum (3,0), origin fixed; left end rises and right end falls. Guides and all source numerical labels retained.

spec.description: Straight left branch joined to a curved right branch; qualitative curve reconstructed without assigning an equation.
spec.mathematics: Straight branch through (-1,0) and (0,1); curved branch from (0,1) to minimum (1,0), through (2,1), then rising. Dashed guides at (2,1), labels x=-1,1,2 and y=1; both ends arrowed.

answer.short: Reflection in the $x$-axis. Join $(0,-1)$; intercepts $(-1,0)$ and $(1,0)$; marked point $(2,-1)$.
answer.worked:
Use $(x,y)\mapsto(x,-y)$.
$$\begin{aligned}(-1,0)&\mapsto(-1,0)\\(0,1)&\mapsto(0,-1)\\(1,0)&\mapsto(1,0)\\(2,1)&\mapsto(2,-1)\end{aligned}$$
The straight branch descends to the join at $(0,-1)$. The curved branch rises to a maximum at $(1,0)$, then falls.

spec.description: Exact vertical reflection of both branches and all Bezier controls.
spec.mathematics: Join (0,-1); unchanged roots -1 and 1; curved maximum (1,0); point (2,-1). Straight branch rises to the upper left, curved branch falls to the lower right.

answer.short: Reflection in both axes. Join $(0,-1)$; intercepts $(-1,0)$ and $(1,0)$; marked point $(-2,-1)$.
answer.worked:
Reflect in both axes using $(x,y)\mapsto(-x,-y)$, equivalent to a $180^\circ$ rotation about the origin.
$$\begin{aligned}(-1,0)&\mapsto(1,0)\\(0,1)&\mapsto(0,-1)\\(1,0)&\mapsto(-1,0)\\(2,1)&\mapsto(-2,-1)\end{aligned}$$
The curved branch is on the left, with a maximum at $(-1,0)$. The straight branch rises from $(0,-1)$ through $(1,0)$.

spec.description: Both-axis reflection of the complete supplied piecewise curve.
spec.mathematics: Curved left branch through (-2,-1), maximum (-1,0), join (0,-1); straight right branch through (1,0). All points and control points undergo (x,y) to (-x,-y).

spec.description: Increasing qualitative S-shaped curve with horizontal asymptotes, drawn without inferring an equation.
spec.mathematics: Passes through (-1,-1), (0,0), (1,1); approaches y=-2 on the left and y=2 on the right from between the asymptotes. Dashed coordinate guides and all source numerical labels retained. Arrowed ends indicate continuation.

answer.short: Decreasing S-shaped graph through $(-1,1)$, $(0,0)$ and $(1,-1)$; asymptotes $y=2$ on the left and $y=-2$ on the right.
answer.worked:
Reflect in the $y$-axis using $(x,y)\mapsto(-x,y)$.
$$\begin{aligned}(-1,-1)&\mapsto(1,-1)\\(0,0)&\mapsto(0,0)\\(1,1)&\mapsto(-1,1)\end{aligned}$$
The horizontal asymptotes remain $y=\pm2$. Their left and right approaches interchange, giving a decreasing S-shaped graph.

spec.description: Exact horizontal reflection of the base curve and every control point.
spec.mathematics: Decreasing through (-1,1), origin and (1,-1); approaches y=2 on the left and y=-2 on the right. Asymptotes and coordinate guides retained.

answer.short: Increasing S-shaped graph through $(-1,-1)$, $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$; asymptotes $y=-2$ on the left and $y=2$ on the right. The supplied sketch is unchanged.
answer.worked:
Reflect in both axes using $(x,y)\mapsto(-x,-y)$.
$$\begin{aligned}(-1,-1)&\mapsto(1,1)\\(0,0)&\mapsto(0,0)\\(1,1)&\mapsto(-1,-1)\end{aligned}$$
The asymptotes interchange under the vertical reflection, while the horizontal reflection interchanges the left and right ends. The result is an increasing S-shaped graph with the same appearance as the supplied sketch.

spec.description: Both-axis reflection of the complete base curve, retaining its qualitative rotational symmetry.
spec.mathematics: Increasing through (-1,-1), origin and (1,1); approaches y=-2 on the left and y=2 on the right. Every base point and control point undergoes (x,y) to (-x,-y).
